children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices traded in a narrow range on Tuesday after weather forecasts turned milder, easing concerns over strong winter demand that had pushed prices to 10-day highs in the previous session.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was €0.32 higher at €90.08 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0958 GMT, ICE data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) rose by 0.41 pence to 223.68 pence per therm.

The market initially rallied on forecasts of significantly colder long-range weather. But it reversed course after updated model runs pointed to a warmer outlook across Northwest Europe through the remainder of the forecast horizon, said LSEG analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich. "Balanced fundamentals leave us sideways," he said.

Temperatures are still expected to remain below seasonal norms through next week, keeping heating demand elevated, but stronger wind generation and rising French nuclear output are helping offset gas consumption in the power sector.

Northwest European local distribution zone demand, which refers to residential gas demand for heating, is forecast at 4,512 gigawatt hours per day on the day-ahead. Non-LDZ demand of gas for power generation is seen at 3,260 GWh/d, LSEG data showed.

On the supply side, Norwegian exports to continental Europe remain constrained by outages at the Dvalin and Sleipner fields, while maintenance continues at Visund and Ormen Lange. Total Norwegian exports are nominated at around 329 million cubic metres per day on Tuesday and are forecast to rise to 332 mcm/d on the day-ahead.

Despite the softer near-term outlook, analysts at Goldman Sachs said colder-than-average weather and lingering uncertainty over Middle East LNG supply could still tighten the market later this winter, potentially pushing TTF prices above 100 euros/MWh in a prolonged cold-weather scenario.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract was down €0.08 at €82.67 per metric ton.
Warmer Northwest Europe forecasts eased an earlier weather-driven rally
Stronger wind output and higher French nuclear generation are limiting gas use in power
Goldman Sachs says prolonged cold weather could push TTF gas above €100 per megawatt hour
